worksheetTitle: Atomic Structure: Subatomic Particles, Notation & Electronic Arrangement

questions.qText: What strictly determines the identity of a chemical element?
options: The total mass of the atom

questions.qText: An atom is represented by the notation ²⁷₁₃Al. How many neutrons are present in this atom?
A neutral atom of potassium has a proton number of 19 and a nucleon number of 39. How many electrons does it contain?
A particle has 17 protons, 18 neutrons, and 18 electrons. Which of the following statements correctly describes this particle?
options: It is a neutral atom of Chlorine.
It is a neutral atom of Argon.
It is a positively charged particle of the element Chlorine.
It is a negatively charged particle of the element Chlorine.

questions.qText: An element has a proton number of 15. What is its electronic configuration?
An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 8, 2. Which Group of the Periodic Table does it belong to?
An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 3. In which Period of the Periodic Table is this element located?
In the standard atomic notation ᴬZX, what does the symbol 'Z' represent?
An atom has a nucleon number of 23 and contains 11 electrons. Assuming it is a neutral atom, how many neutrons does it have?
Why is the proton number used to identify an element, rather than the nucleon number or electron number?
options: The number of protons is unique to each element and never changes for that element.
The number of electrons is always greater than the number of protons.
The nucleon number is the same for all elements.
Protons are the only subatomic particles that have mass.

questions.qText: An atom has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 7. How many valence (outer shell) electrons does it have, and what does this indicate?
options: 2 valence electrons; it is in Group 2.
8 valence electrons; it is a noble gas.
7 valence electrons; it is in Group 17.
17 valence electrons; it is highly reactive.

questions.qText: A particle has 11 protons and 10 electrons. What is its overall charge and which element does it belong to?
An element is located in Period 2 and Group 15 of the Periodic Table. What is its proton number?
Which of the following atoms contains exactly 10 neutrons?
What is the electronic configuration of a neutral atom with a proton number of 20?
Two different elements have the same number of outer shell electrons. What can be deduced about these two elements?
options: They are in the same Period.
They have the same nucleon number.
They are in the same Group.
They have the same number of protons.
